title: T-B interactions yield CD3B cells and CD20T cells with pathogenic features in multiple sclerosis.
publicationName: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
journalName: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
snippet: Classically, B and T cells are differentiated by their mutually exclusive expression of surface markers such as CD3 and CD20, but it is now established that a few percent of T cells in human blood display also CD20.
